name: Steven Qi
role: Economic & Research Analyst, International Monetary Fund (IMF)
bio: Steven Qi is a Country Analyst in the African Department at the International Monetary Fund (IMF), where he advises the Mission Chiefs and country teams on critical economic policy and analytical output of key IMF country programs. Previously, Steven worked with UN agencies such as UNFPA, where he focused on strategic communications, stakeholder engagement, and humanitarian affairs. He has spoken at institutions including United Nations Headquarters, the World Bank, and Cambridge University. His work bridges economics, diplomacy, and community impact, driven by a passion for connecting people, ideas, and opportunities across borders to deliver lasting positive change.

name: Tyler E. Tucker
role: Special Advisor to the Chief Executive Officer, Elizabeth Dole Foundation
bio: Tyler advances the strategic priorities of the Elizabeth Dole Foundation, working to empower and support the nation’s 14.3 million military and veteran caregivers who care for our servicemembers and veterans. As Special Advisor, he leads executive office operations, engages key stakeholders, and champions staff development and growth.

name: Ayushi Mohanty
role: Data Engineer, Mastercard
bio: Ayushi is a data engineer at Mastercard, where she builds data pipelines and infrastructure to support the company's Fortune 500 cleint engagements. She is passionate about using technology to drive social impact and has experience working on projects related to equitable technology adoption. Ayushi is also an advocate for diversity and inclusion in the tech industry and is committed to creating opportunities for underrepresented groups in technology.

name: Christian Gyles Ramos
role: Operations and Special Projects Associate (APIA Scholars)
bio:
Christian Gyles Ramos is an Operations and Special Projects Associate at APIA Scholars. He plays a proactive role in supporting multiple departments by assisting with various projects and administrative tasks, while advocating for resources that advance AANHPI students in higher education. Previously, Christian served as a Congressional Intern for the Office of Representative Judy Chu (CA-28) and as an Office Intern for the Asian Pacific American Institute for Congressional Studies (APAICS). 
 Christian is a proud first-generation college graduate from the University of Guam, where he earned a Bachelor of Business Administration degree and was recognized as a 2023 Truman Scholar. After graduation, he continued to further his passion for public service in Washington, D.C. through volunteering with APAICS, SMYAL, Truman Scholars Association, Global Shapers (Washington, D.C. Hub), and Men4Choice. 
 With a deep passion and commitment for public service, he constantly strives to uplift the voices of AANHPI, LGBTQ+, and first-generation, low-income (FGLI) students everywhere. As an LGBTQ+ son of Filipino immigrant parents and from an economically disadvantaged background, Christian has witnessed firsthand the systemic disparities that hinder individuals from having a fair opportunity at life. These experiences fuel his passion for social justice, inspire him to create meaningful change, and champion policies that uplift marginalized communities everywhere. He hopes to pursue an MPA and/or JD to further his commitment and drive to advocate for equitable access to affordable housing, healthcare, education, and food security for low-income families and marginalized communities.

name: Anthony Johnson
role: Head of Portfolio Strategy, Tenable
bio: Anthony Johnson is a corporate strategy and public affairs leader committed to leveraging technology and community collaboration to build a safer and more equitable society. At Tenable, he leads strategic global business initiatives that equip organizations with AI-powered cybersecurity solutions to protect IT, cloud, and critical infrastructure. A trusted advisor to senior executives and civil society organizations, Anthony brings a global perspective shaped by previous leadership roles held at Bain & Company, Siemens, and UN Human Rights. He holds degrees from the University of Cincinnati and The London School of Economics. He currently resides in Washington, DC with his wife Amanda and two cats, Athena and Rhea.

name: Akash Mehta
role: Environmental Specialist, World Bank
bio:
Akash Mehta is an Environmental Specialist at the World Bank Group's Environment Department. In this capacity, he focuses on integrating cutting-edge technologies such as geospatial analytics, GIS and artificial intelligence into development projects, primarily through his support for the Knowledge, Information & Data Services Helpdesk. With nearly a decade of experience spanning the public and academic sectors, he has contributed to various environmental initiatives, including drought and flood monitoring, biodiversity conservation, and landscape restoration. Beyond his operational duties, Akash supports several flagship global initiatives, including the Livable Planet Observatory, Extended Producer Responsibility for Plastics, Africa Eurasian Flyway Initiative and Accelerating Access to Clean Air. 
 Prior to the World Bank, Akash held positions with the University of Cambridge, the governments of Senegal and India, and the Reserve Bank of India. He holds a Master of Public Administration in International Development from the London School of Economics and a Bachelor of Economics (Honors) from Shri Ram College of Commerce. Outside of work, Akash is an avid nature enthusiast and enjoys playing squash.

name: Kathleen Schwind
role: Engagement Manager,McKinsey & Co.
bio: Kathleen Schwind is a leader at the intersection of defense, diplomacy, and global business. At McKinsey & Co., she leads geopolitics, defense, and supply chain resilience teams, driving defense industrial base transformations, aligning senior international partners on first-of-its-kind multilateral agreements, and shaping executive-level decisions amid complex geopolitical landscapes.

name: Olivia Solomon
role: Georgetown University Masters of Urban and Regional Planning
bio: Olivia is earning her masters degree in Urban and Regional Planning at Georgetown University. She is utilizing her past experience of political organizing to specialize in community planning and housing policy. She seeks to use her degree to reform or housing system and create and better future for all.

name: Shahaan Mirza
role: Assurety Consulting & Solutions; Head of AI & Product Innovation
bio: Shahaan is an operator with a background in venture capital, startup mentorship, and early-stage business building. As Head of AI & Product Innovation, he oversees AI governance, strategy, and manages several products across Assurety's enterprise suite in the AI and Business Intelligence category. In his free time, he advises early stage startups, and leads TownHallOS, a 501(c)3 think tank helping civic orgs and nonprofits understand policy in real community context. He manages uncertainty, and unites purpose-driven people to create successful outcomes.

name: Elena Anthie Sarigeorgiou
role: International Studies Undergraduate, American University
bio:
Elena Sarigeorgiou is a senior at American University's School of International Service, where she studies International Studies with a focus on the intersection of youth engagement, policy, and global development. Her work centers on how institutions design and implement policy affecting young people, with attention to education systems, and the role of youth in shaping more inclusive and accountable instituions. 
 She has contributed to policy research and programming across nonprofit, government, and multilateral contexts. As an Intern the Aspen Institute, she supported research and convenings on philanthropy and the nonprofit sector. She also works with the DMUN Foundation, where she has drafted policy briefs on youth participation and economic development. Her previous experience includes contributing to a policy report on youth engagement at the Delaware Department of Education and leading advocacy initiatives on girls' education with an international civil society organization. 
 Across her work, Elena has developed a strong foundation in policy research, writing, and stakeholder engagement, with a particular interest in how youth perspectives can move beyond consultation to meaningful influence in decision-making processes.

name: Valerie Aguilar Dellisanti
role: Senior Analyst, 57 Stars
bio: Valerie Aguilar Dellisanti (Peru, 24 years old) is a tech diplomacy advocate and investment professional, working in the international finance industry in the Washington D.C. area. She moved to the DMV after graduating from Brown University in 2023. She is currently an incoming dual degree candidate at the Stanford Graduate School of Business and the Harvard Kennedy School. In her free time, Valerie loves dancing, music, learning languages, and traveling the world.

name: Alexandra Kaiss
role: Senior International Trade Specialist, Cassidy Levy Kent
bio:
Alexandra Kaiss is a Senior International Trade Specialist at Cassidy Levy Kent in Washington, D.C. Her work supports the representation of governments and companies in trade litigation before U.S. agencies and courts, while also advising clients on navigating complex regulatory trade environments. 
 Alexandra was selected as the American Young Trade Leader at the World Trade Organization—one of seven participants globally—where she works to advance youth perspectives in multilateral trade discussions and promote greater understanding of the WTO's work in the United States. She also serves on the Albrecht Fellowship Advisory Board at the World Trade Center Institute, helping shape youth-driven programming focused on international business and diplomacy. 
 She received her B.A. in International Relations and a Certificate in Advanced Leadership Studies from American University in 2023, with additional studies completed at Sciences Po.

name: Sophia N. Wallace
role: Senior Program Associate for the International Partners, Aspen Institute
bio: Sophia Wallace is a Senior Program Associate with the Aspen Institute International Partners, where she manages institutional partnerships and global initiatives across a network of 13 Aspen Institutes worldwide. Her work focuses on leadership and emerging global challenges, leading international initiatives that convene policymakers, experts, and emerging leaders across sectors. She has led major international initiatives including the 2024 NATO Youth Summit and founded the Global Changemakers Workshop, a leadership initiative that convenes emerging leaders from around the world to engage critical challenges shaping democracy, governance, and security. Prior to Aspen, Sophia worked with the U.S. Department of State’s Bureau of European and Eurasian Affairs and supported refugee resettlement efforts through Catholic Charities Refugee and Migration Services. Sophia holds a Bachelor of Arts in Government and International Politics, with a minor in International Security, from George Mason University, where she graduated summa cum laude. She is an incoming M.A. candidate in International Relations at Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies concentrating in Security, Strategy, and Statecraft, a member of the Pi Sigma Alpha National Political Science Honor Society, and a member of the Washington, DC Hub of the Global Shapers Community.

name: Evan Wayne
role: Program Manager for Impact at the Andrew Goodman Foundation
bio: Evan Wayne  is a native of Smyrna, Georgia. He is a 2020 graduate of Georgia State University with a degree in Public Policy, a minor in Cello Performance, and an inductee to Georgia State University’s 2022 40 under 40 class. At GSU, Evan was a founding member of his  Vote Everywhere, where he led civic engagement programming on campus. While pursuing his undergraduate studies, Evan served as a Summer Research Fellow at the United States Department of Defense, serving at the Pentagon. At the Pentagon, Evan worked in legislative affairs and worked to supported the DOD Office of General Counsel. Upon graduating, Evan became a 2020 Puffin Fellow with the Andrew Goodman Foundation. Evan founded the Georgia Youth Poll Worker Project, recruiting 1,000 poll workers for the 2020 general election and 2021 runoff.  The ACLU of Georgia officially acquired the Georgia Youth Poll Worker Project in December 2021, naming him a Voter Access Project Fellow between December 2021 and September 2023. As a fellow, Evan worked to protect on-campus early voting centers in Atlanta and supported ACLU GA's legislative initiatives.  Evan is a writer who has published in publications such as Forbes, Teen Vogue, and the Atlanta Journal-Constitution. After leaving the ACLU of Georgia, Evan served as the Managing Organizer of Georgia for Our Turn, where he worked with APS students to create a student mental health community board district-wide. During the 2024 election season, Evan worked as a VoteFlare Associate at the Shorenstein Center for Media and Politics at the Harvard Kennedy School and as the Religious Outreach advisor for Congresswoman Lucy McBath's Campaign. Evan served as the Senior Economic Policy Advisor at the Netherlands Consulate in Atlanta. Finally, Evan works as the Program Manager for Impact with the Andrew Goodman Foundation and the Atlanta Liaison for StartAruba.

name: Paul Kruchoski
role: Director, Guidehouse
bio:
Paul Kruchoski is a Director at Guidehouse, where he helps government agencies modernize operations and leverage emerging technologies. 
 Previously, he served as a senior U.S. diplomat and career member of the Senior Executive Service. In his final role at the State Department, he served as the chief operating officer for public diplomacy, managing a $1.5 billion budget and 5,000 person global organization. He won the State Department's Sean Smith Award for Innovation in the Use of Technology. Prior assignments include creating and leading the Public Diplomacy Research and Evaluation Unit (REU), Deputy Director of the Collaboratory Innovation Unit, Special Assistant in the Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, and several positions in the Bureau of International Organization Affairs. 
 He is a term member of the Council on Foreign Relations and a graduate of the University of Cincinnati. Outside of his work, Paul is an accomplished cellist.

name: Moritz Ludwig
role: Protocol Officer & Social Secretary to the Ambassador, German Embassy
bio: Moritz supports Ambassador Jens Hanefeld in planning and executing diplomatic engagements to advance transatlantic partnerships and coordination. He holds a Bachelor's degree in International Relations and is a Georgetown Master of Public Policy graduate.

name: Avyan Mejdeen
role: Asylum Officer, USCIS
bio: Avyan serves as an Asylum Officer with the U.S. federal government, where she adjudicates complex claims from individuals fleeing persecution. She conducts rigorous, in-depth interviews to elicit survivors' accounts of trauma and displacement, weighs evidence against exacting legal standards, and renders determinations with life-altering consequences, approaching the work as a form of advocacy that ensures people fleeing danger are heard fully, treated with dignity, and judged fairly under the law.

name: Arshita Sandhiparthi
role: J.D. Candidate, Georgetown Law
bio: Arshita is a former cybersecurity professional turned law student at Georgetown Law. She hopes to make sense of our digital era through technology-related impact litigation after graduating with her J.D.

name: Melissa Shambach
role: Policy Analyst, RAND
bio: Melissa Shambach is a policy analyst at RAND focusing on emerging technology, crisis response, and geopolitics. Prior to RAND she worked as an innovation consultant for the U.S. government, a trainee at NATO, and as a project coordinator for a number of humanitarian NGOs internationally.

name: Diyora Shodmonova
role: MBA Candidate, George Washington University School of Business
bio: Diyora is an MBA candidate driven to build high-impact initiatives at the intersection of education, technology, and international engagement. As Managing Director of the Harvard Youth Leadership Summit, an initiative of the Harvard Project for Asian and International Relations (HPAIR), she directed the first Harvard youth leadership summit hosted in Central Asia, bringing global dialogue directly to her home region. She thrives on connecting communities across borders, fostering cross-cultural collaboration, and opening new pathways for young leaders to shape global conversations.

name: Charlotte Elisa Levy Kennedy
role: Program Manager, Latin America Leadership Program, Georgetown University
bio: Charlotte leads Georgetown University's Latin America Leadership Program (LALP) executive education programs: Global Competitiveness Leadership (GCL), Innovation and Leadership in Government (ILG), and Global Business Executive Leadership (GBEL). She oversees the planning and implementation of these annual initiatives, which are designed to educate, connect, and inspire regional leaders to build networks that generate a positive multiplier effect across Latin America and the Caribbean.

name: Isabela Valencia
role: Content Coordinator, Aspen Institute
bio: Isabela is a climate and environmental policy professional with experience advising foundations, governments, and NGOs on climate action, governance, and sustainable development. She is a Content Coordinator with the Aspen Institute's Energy and Environment Program and also serves as the Deputy Director of Research at Climate Cardinals. Her experience spans philanthropy and climate, land use and energy policy. She holds a Master of Environmental Management from Yale University and a Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Studies from Wellesley College.

name: Carson Tighe
role: Senior Associate, Capital Markets and Risk, Capital One
bio: Carson supports the Capital Markets and Risk organization at Capital One, helping strengthen how the company identifies, assesses, and manages technology risk. As a Senior Associate on the Finance Risk Management team, he works with business and technology partners to evaluate controls, navigate change, and promote effective risk management. Outside of his professional work, Carson serves on the board of First Tee Shenandoah Valley and is pursuing a Master of Science in Analytics at Georgia Tech.

name: Yondonjamts Batzorigt
role: Design Engineer, Arlington County Government
bio: Graduated from Penn State University in Civil Engineering. Currently working at Arlington County Government as a Design Engineer. Whether it's designing safer streets, exploring ways to increase housing opportunities, or volunteering in my community, I'm passionate about creating practical solutions with lasting impact.

name: Vannia Anais Cabrera Aldana
role: MBA Student, Georgetown University
bio: Vannia Cabrera Aldana is a Fulbright Scholar and incoming MBA candidate at Georgetown University with a background in global financial operations at HSBC. Deeply connected to her Mexican heritage, she has spearheaded social initiatives aimed at empowering indigenous communities, protecting ancestral craftsmanship, and building sustainable economic autonomy for rural families. Driven by a lifelong fascination with global cultures, Vannia has cultivated an international perspective through immersive experiences, ranging from studying Mandarin during an academic exchange in Taiwan to serving as a diplomatic liaison at UNESCO MONDIACULT. As a Global Shaper, she is committed to combining technology, inclusive finance, and cross-cultural collaboration to ensure underrepresented communities thrive on the global stage.

name: Rudra Saigal
role: M.A. Candidate in International Economics and Finance, Johns Hopkins SAIS
bio: Rudra Saigal is a graduate student in International Economics and Finance at Johns Hopkins SAIS, focusing on geoeconomics, development finance, and economic statecraft. He serves as Finance Policy Rapporteur at the Helsinki Geoeconomics Society, where his work examines monetary fragmentation, sanctions, sovereign hedging, and global financial governance. Previously, he worked at the United Nations Secretariat in New York on sustainable finance and with NITI Aayog in India on development policy. Rudra graduated magna cum laude and Phi Beta Kappa as a Presidential Scholar from the University of Southern California where he majored in Economics. At USC, he served as Speaker of the Undergraduate Student Senate and co-founded Students for South Asia, a student-led coalition that successfully advocated for the establishment of the university's South Asian Studies minor. He was also awarded the Order of the Laurel and the Palm, USC's highest student honor.

name: Xavier Lopez
role: Senior Manager, Membership, Future Caucus
bio: Xavier Lopez manages membership and oversees State Future Caucuses for a growing national network of over 2,100+ young legislators, providing unique opportunities, tools, and resources for these policymakers to forge productive bipartisan partnerships on critical national issues across state and party lines.

name: Luiz Antonio Cardoso dos Santos
role: Information Systems Consultant, IDB
bio: Luiz supports digital transformation initiatives at the Inter-American Development Bank, working on the technology systems and processes that keep institutional operations running efficiently. With a background spanning mechatronics engineering, consulting, and fintech, he focuses on identifying where technology and AI can streamline workflows and improve how organizations operate day to day.

name: Brett Schreiner
role: Administrative Coordinator, International Monetary Fund
bio: At the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Brett is a part of the Special Office Support (SOS) team, a unique division which supports the operations workflow of numerous Fund departments on ad-hoc bases. Brett is highly passionate about international development and development economics, and formerly supported the project management of numerous USAID contracts.

name: Griffin Henry
role: Student, George Mason University Carter School for Peace and Conflict Resolution
bio: Griffin is a conflict resolution student completing an accelerated B.S./M.A. in Conflict Analysis and Resolution at George Mason University's Carter School for Peace and Conflict Resolution, with the B.S. expected Spring 2027 and the M.A. expected Fall 2028. His work spans peacebuilding, human rights, and policy research, including prior roles supporting the Executive Office at Human Rights First and Senator Tim Kaine's Office. Griffin is especially interested in foreign assistance, PeaceTech, and cross-sector collaboration.

name: Maya Khachab
role: Junior Research Fellow, Environment, Climate Change, and Security Program, NATO Association of Canada
bio: Maya Khachab is a Junior Research Fellow in the Environment, Climate Change and Security program at the NATO Association of Canada. Maya's research focuses on the security implications of climate change for Canada's defence priorities and the alliance, examining national disaster response and developing policy proposals for civic preparedness.

name: Sutavee Thaivanich
role: Recent LLM Graduate, Georgetown University Law Center
bio: Sutavee is a human rights and justice-sector professional from Thailand, and she holds an LL.M. in International Legal Studies with an International Human Rights Certificate from Georgetown Law. Her work has spanned justice reform in Thailand, including a reintegration program for incarcerated women and investigative research on civic space and political detention, working alongside government, UN agencies, and civil society on the ground.

name: Janna Tosson
role: Student, George Mason University
bio: Janna Tosson is an undergraduate student pursuing a dual degree in Conflict Analysis and Resolution, with a concentration in Political and Social Action, and Government and International Politics. She also has a minor in Dance Appreciation. Janna has served as the Community Chair of the Carter School Ambassadors since Fall 2024. She is currently a fellow at the Office of Community Engagement and Civic Learning and an undergraduate research assistant. Additionally, she serves as the Executive Director of NLG @ George Mason, a student organization working to make higher education accessible for refugee students, and the Human Security Division Chief for the Sycamore Institute, the first foreign policy and national security-focused undergraduate-run think tank. In these roles, she has gained experience bridging theory with practice. She's passionate about ethical community engagement and the utilization of international law to support grassroots peacebuilding initiatives globally.

name: Joseph Ching
role: Program Manager, Postsecondary Commission
bio: Joseph advances the research and evaluation functions of the Postsecondary Commission, an accreditor dedicated to recognizing innovative colleges that deliver strong economic outcomes. As a Program Manager, he helped launch a groundbreaking study on the value of higher education and supports the Commission's petition to receive federal recognition from the U.S. Department of Education.

name: Taylor Coleman
role: Legislative Affairs Specialist, DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection
bio: Taylor Coleman serves the DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection as a Legislative Affairs Specialist. In this capacity, she advises on political strategy and tracks legislation for the agency. Previously, she served Councilmember Christina Henderson in several capacities at the DC Council for three and a half years. During her tenure in Councilmember Henderson's office, Taylor oversaw multiple committees and advanced the legislative priorities of the Committee on Health. Her portfolio included health, consumer protection, scope of practice reform, data privacy, education, parks and recreation, and disability services. Before joining the DC Council, Taylor worked as an Elections Research Assistant at Global Strategy Group, a public opinion firm. In that role, she developed slide decks, memos, and dashboards to communicate analytical insights and trends to Democratic candidates. She earned her Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from Georgia State University. In her free time, Taylor enjoys watching horror movies, trying new restaurants, and listening to 80s pop and 70s R&B.

name: Angie Cherikos
role: Senior Coordinator, Community Engagement, Elizabeth Dole Foundation
bio: Angie Cherikos serves as the Senior Coordinator, Caregiver Engagement, supporting the efficiency and organization of the Elizabeth Dole Foundation. She joined EDF in late September 2024, bringing a deep personal connection to the military community as part of a Marine family. From 2023 to 2024, Angie participated in the Blue Star Families DEPLOY Fellowship program, where she led the Spaces for Belonging initiative, designed to foster community for LGBTQ+ military children. Prior to transitioning to the military support field, Angie worked as a certified dog trainer and adoptions counselor at Washington, DC's animal shelter. A 2021 graduate of the University of Mary Washington with a degree in Psychology, Angie also competed as a track athlete. She currently lives in Washington, DC, with her dog, and spends her free time running, reading, and exploring new restaurants with friends. Angie is thrilled to be part of an organization that supports military families like her own.

name: Naomi Garcia-Hector
role: Campaigns Associate, Center for American Progress Action Fund
bio: Naomi Garcia-Hector is a Campaigns Associate at the Center for American Progress Action Fund, where her work sits at the intersection of policy and people. She supports CAP Action's Storytelling Program, sourcing, vetting, and training storytellers across the country whose lives have been upended by policy decisions in Congress. Her work focuses on getting stories in front of the press, partners, and platforms that can carry them furthest, making the human stakes of policy decisions impossible to ignore and building the public pressure needed to drive change. She holds a degree in public policy from Georgia State University, and outside of work can be found growing her plant collection or training in Muay Thai.
